# Champions of the Future

**Champions of the Future** (COTF) is an international kart racing competition organized by the RGMMC Group and sanctioned by the CIK-FIA (Commission Internationale de Karting). Established in 2020, the series serves as a preparatory platform for drivers competing in the FIA Karting European and World Championships. The events are typically scheduled two weeks prior to FIA Karting events at the same circuits, allowing teams and drivers to test equipment and familiarize themselves with track conditions under competitive regulations .

The competition encompasses several distinct series, including the **Champions of the Future Euro Series**, the **Champions of the Future Shifters**, and the **Champions of the Future Academy Program**. The latter, launched in 2023, utilizes an "arrive-and-drive" format aimed at cost containment and talent identification, featuring a partnership with the F1 Academy to promote female participation in motorsport .

In late 2025, the organization announced significant expansions scheduled for 2026, including the launch of regional series in the United Kingdom and the United States, as well as a Formula 4 development program .

## History

### Foundation and Early Years (2020–2022)
Champions of the Future was founded in 2020 by the RGMMC Group, a Swiss-based motorsport promoter responsible for organizing FIA Karting events . The series was created to fill a gap in the calendar for high-level international testing races. The inaugural season in 2020 faced scheduling disruptions due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The opening round, originally planned for Wackersdorf, Germany, in May, was cancelled. The series eventually debuted in Zuera, Spain, in July 2020, followed by a round in Portimão, Portugal .

The initial format focused on the CIK-FIA direct-drive classes: OK (Senior) and OK-Junior (OK-J), alongside the gearbox class KZ2 and the 60 Mini category . Notable inaugural champions included Nikita Bedrin (OK) and Arvid Lindblad (OK-Junior) .

In 2022, the organization hosted a one-off "Winter Series" at the Franciacorta Karting Track in Italy prior to the main season. The regular season was subsequently rebranded as the **Champions of the Future Euro Series** .

### Expansion and Academy Program (2023–Present)
In 2023, RGMMC expanded the brand by launching the **Champions of the Future Academy Program (COTFA)**. Unlike the Euro Series, which relies on factory teams and private entrants bringing their own equipment, the Academy Program was designed as an "arrive-and-drive" series. This format requires drivers to use supplied chassis and engines allocated via a lottery system to ensure parity and reduce costs .

The Academy Program introduced the OK-N and OK-N Junior categories to the international stage, alongside the Mini 60 class. The series gained prominence through a collaboration with the F1 Academy's "Discover Your Drive" initiative, headed by Susie Wolff. This partnership provides financial support and equipment to selected female drivers in each category to foster diversity in the sport .

In 2024, Luna Fluxá became the first female driver to win a Champions of the Future title, securing the Academy Program's OK-N Senior championship .

## Series Structure and Categories

As of 2025, the competition is divided into three primary international championships, with additional national and development programs in development.

### Euro Series
The Euro Series is the premier tier of the competition, designed for elite international teams and drivers. It functions as the primary testing ground for the FIA Karting European and World Championships.
* **Classes:** OK (Senior), OK-Junior.
* **Format:** The calendar typically consists of five rounds held at major European circuits such as Valencia (Spain), Val d'Argenton (France), and Kristianstad (Sweden) .
* **Regulations:** The series strictly follows CIK-FIA technical regulations to ensure data relevance for upcoming FIA events .

### Shifters
Dedicated to gearbox karting, the Shifters series features the KZ categories.
* **Classes:** KZ, KZ2, and KZ2 Masters.
* **Format:** Events are often held as standalone weekends or in conjunction with specific Euro Series rounds, depending on the FIA calendar alignment .

### Academy Program
The Academy Program focuses on talent development and accessibility.
* **Classes:** Mini 60 (ages 8–12), OK-N Junior (ages 12–14), and OK-N Senior (ages 15+) .
* **Equipment:** Drivers utilize CIK-FIA homologated equipment provided by the organizers. Chassis and engines are drawn by lottery to equalize performance .
* **F1 Academy Partnership:** The "Discover Your Drive" initiative supports three female drivers in each class, providing branded karts, race suits, and entry fee subsidies .

### F4 Racing Academy
In September 2025, RGMMC launched the **Champions of the Future Racing Academy**, a Formula 4 development program. Led by racing driver Augusto Farfus, the program is designed for drivers in their final year of karting. It offers a year-long testing schedule with a dedicated car, engineer, and coach for eight selected drivers, aiming to bridge the gap between karting and single-seater racing .

## 2025 Season and Results

The 2025 season saw the Euro Series conclude in September at the Åsum Ring in Kristianstad, Sweden.

* **OK Category:** British driver **Kenzo Craigie** (Prema Racing) secured the championship title. Although the final race in Kristianstad was won by Daniel Kelleher, Craigie's consistent performance throughout the season allowed him to secure the overall victory with 333 points .
* **OK-Junior Category:** **Noah Baglin** (Prema Racing) won the title after a double victory in the final round, winning both the Final and the championship. He overcame a points deficit to defeat William Calleja .

In the Shifters category, the season featured rounds in Valencia and Franciacorta. The champions included Senna van Walstijn (KZ), Maksim Orlov (KZ2), and Angelo Lombardo (KZ2-Masters) .

## Controversies

### 2025 Valencia Tyre Boycott
In May 2025, the Champions of the Future Shifters round in Valencia, Spain, was disrupted by a driver boycott in the KZ category. Competitors expressed dissatisfaction with the performance and consistency of the control tires provided by Dunlop, which had been mandated for the event and the subsequent European Championship .

Drivers claimed the tires lacked grip and created safety concerns, stating that the premier KZ class was lapping slower than junior categories. A petition signed by major drivers, including several World Champions, requested a switch to alternative manufacturers such as LeCont or Vega. When the request was not granted, the majority of the KZ field refused to participate in the final race. Only 11 karts started the final, and only three drivers completed the race . Following the incident, the CIK-FIA dropped Dunlop as a supplier for the category .

## Future Expansion (2026)

The organization has announced a significant global expansion of the Academy Program model for the 2026 season.

### Champions of the Future America
In partnership with **K1 Speed**, a large indoor karting operator, and the RGMMC Group, a new series titled **Champions of the Future America** is scheduled to launch in 2026. The series aims to create a pathway for American drivers to international competition. The 2026 season will feature ten rounds, primarily based in the Southwestern United States, utilizing circuits such as the K1 Circuit in Winchester, California .

### British Champions of the Future Academy
In collaboration with **Motorsport UK**, the governing body for motorsport in the United Kingdom, a national version of the Academy Program will launch in 2026. The series will take place across four UK locations and will utilize the same lottery-based equipment model (Parolin/TM for Mini, Kart Republic/IAME for OK-N classes) as the international series. This initiative is part of the Motorsport UK Karting Pathway .

### Middle East and Asia
The series continues to expand its footprint in the Middle East and Asia, with events planned in the United Arab Emirates and a specific title event in Macau .

## Notable Champions

The series has featured numerous drivers who have progressed to single-seater racing and Formula One junior academies.

**_Luna Fluxa Cross made history by clinching the inaugural Champions of the Future Academy Program OK-N Senior class title in dominant fashion, with six final wins, nine podiums, and a remarkable display of speed and consistency throughout the season._**

![Image 1: Alice Buckley, Bridgestone GR86 Championship, 2024 Taupo](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/aed0c4_8dc7509d632a4659adadb038c9a07ba8~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_147,h_92,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/aed0c4_8dc7509d632a4659adadb038c9a07ba8~mv2.jpg)

Photo credits: Mercedes

Luna Fluxa Cross, 14, made history as she claimed her sixth final win of the season and, in doing so, was crowned the inaugural champion in the Champions of the Future Academy Program (COTFA) in the Senior class, the top category in the RGMMC-promoted series.

A Mercedes Junior driver with an outstanding record in national and international karting across classes, Fluxa became the first female driver to win an FIA International championship since 1966, when Susanna Raganelli became Karting World Champion.

Fluxa—who is also part of the Iron Dames program—was a dominant force all season, claiming five out of six wins in the first half of the season. She then returned to the top step of the podium at Al Forsan, Abu Dhabi, which hosted the final round of the inaugural year for the series.

Created with the support of F1 Academy's _Discover Your Drive_ initiative, the series aims to develop and foster female talent in a high-level, mixed-gender, yet cost-effective environment. F1 Academy announced it would support three female drivers in each class—and Fluxa repaid the trust with an outstanding campaign that saw the Spaniard taking the crown with one race to spare, in a field of over 45 elite karters who entered at least one round.

Returning to the track where the Champions of the Future Academy program was launched last year, Fluxa was at the top of her game again. She showed the same pace that had marked her dominant first half of the season, building on the speed she displayed in the OK-Junior class during her first appearance as an F1 Academy-supported racer.

An unbelievable run in the European legs of the championship saw Fluxa lose only one final—Valencia's second race—where she still claimed second place. Dominant in every round on every track, Fluxa maintained her strong form as the series headed to the Middle East, where she encountered some bad luck but consistently battled at the front in every race.

After a DNF took her out for the first time at Al Ain in the penultimate round, she bounced back with a third-place Race 2. Entering the season finale at Al Forsan Circuit with a healthy margin, she remained comfortably in control of the championship standings.

At the Abu Dhabi facility, it was business as usual for Fluxa. Straight from practice, she was consistently among the top three in the timesheets in every session. She qualified second for the first day's heats, clocking a 55.243-second lap.

In the first heat on Tuesday, starting from the front row, Fluxa was pushed to the outside line and dropped to third behind her closest rival in the standings, Hugo Herrouin. As she tried to charge back, Markas Silkunas also found a way past; despite losing some ground, Fluxa remained focused. By lap six, she overtook Herrouin to reclaim third and began pressuring Silkunas, clocking the fastest laps of the race. Though unable to pass the fast Lithuanian, Fluxa settled for third, in a smart drive given her championship lead.

In the second heat, Fluxa had a cautious start and dropped to fourth as she avoided chaos in turn one. Knowing she only needed a start from the front-rows for the final to unleash her pace, she focused on staying consistent. She engaged in good battles with Gale and Mneimneh, passing the latter on lap five to finish fifth. Her performance secured her third place on the grid for the first final.

![Image 2: ree](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/aed0c4_37acb659e725443fb8277307c28d86a1~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_147,h_92,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/aed0c4_37acb659e725443fb8277307c28d86a1~mv2.jpg)

Photo credits: RGMMC

Starting from P3 in the first final of the week, Luna Fluxa lined up behind Daniel Kelleher and Markas Silkunas, with closest title rival Hugo Herrouin in P4.

Fluxa made an excellent start from the inside row, immediately gaining a position to take second place behind Kelleher.

While drivers in the mid-pack engaged in skirmishes that eliminated a few, Fluxa maintained her composure; by the end of the first lap, she made her move on Kelleher and surged into the lead.

Fluxa began to pull away from the pack, but Austin Gale—who had gained two positions off the start—moved into second and started to challenge her. Gale clocked the fastest lap on lap three, briefly closing the gap to Fluxa, who responded with a 55.767 lap to maintain her lead.

For several laps, the battle was tense. Gale was relentless in his pursuit, closing in once again. But Fluxa responded with unmatched consistency, lowering the fastest lap to 55.560 on lap nine. By this point, she had extended her lead to 1.8 seconds.

Herrouin, meanwhile, pushed hard to snatch the fastest lap and the extra championship point, but Fluxa had already built an unassailable gap. With unrelenting pace, Luna crossed the finish line well ahead of the competition, taking her sixth win of the season in dominant fashion.

![Image 3: ree](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/aed0c4_94b3f9aacd884337b86fabd7a2cce1cf~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_147,h_92,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/aed0c4_94b3f9aacd884337b86fabd7a2cce1cf~mv2.jpg)

Photo credits: RGMMC / F1 Academy

With this victory, Fluxa secured the championship title with one race to spare, amassing 629 points — a 127-point margin over Herrouin — and became the inaugural champion of the Champions of the Future Academy Program, further solidifying her position as one of the brightest talents in global karting.

Other notable performances from female drivers in the race included Skye Parker finishing P13, Sofia Zanfari recovering to P16, and Elizaveta Kozlova in P15.

The final day of the championship began with another remarkable performance from Fluxa, as she took pole position in qualifying for the heats, clocking a 54.969 lap which was the fastest anyone had recorded at the Al Forsan circuit throughout the weekend and the first under the 55 second barrier.

In the first heat, Fluxa lost the lead to Hamza Al Fayez at the first corner but kept her cool; she fought back on lap three, engaging in a clean battle with Al Fayez. After trading positions, Fluxa made a decisive move on lap six to secure the lead and, from there she could pull away and take victory with unmatched pace in clear air.

In the second heat, Fluxa had a better start and held off Al Fayez through the opening corners. Silkunas however first moved up into second and eventually passed her to win the heat, but Fluxa’s second-place finish was still enough to secure pole position for the final.

![Image 4: ree](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/aed0c4_ad691443b24f460ba9764e10ac239c61~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_147,h_92,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/aed0c4_ad691443b24f460ba9764e10ac239c61~mv2.jpg)

Photo credits: RGMMC / F1 Academy

The last final of the year was again a showcase of Luna Fluxa’s determination and speed. Starting from pole position after strong qualifying heats, Fluxa shared the front row with Lithuania’s Markas Silkunas, still in competition for second in the standings.

Under the watchful eyes of Susie and Toto Wolff, as well as several F1 Academy drivers observing from the stands, the lights went out. Silkunas had an exceptional getaway and took the lead around the outside as Fluxa was engaged in intense wheel-to-wheel battles.

Hamza Al Fayez, Austin Gale, and Daniel Kelleher all challenged her aggressively into Turn 1 and, in a dramatic chain reaction, Al Fayez spunwent around while attempting to pass Fluxa, triggering a multi-kart crash that also took out Hugo Herrouin, ending his race. Fluxa, momentarily sideways, managed to avoid disaster and regained control, emerging in second place.

Silkunas had taken full advantage of the chaos to build a commanding lead. Fluxa, however, kept her head down and immediately began pushing to close the gap. Behind her, Rafalik and Motlekar capitalized on the early incidents to move into third and fourth, while Fluxa opened a comfortable margin over this chasing group.

Meanwhile, British driver Skye Parker was having a strong race, running in 12th, closely pursued by Sofia Zanfari, who had made an impressive recovery from 21st to 13th by lap two. Further back, Elizaveta Kozlova also avoided the first-lap melee, climbing into the top 15.

By lap three, Fluxa began to showcase her incredible pace, consistently setting the fastest laps. She broke the 56-second barrier on lap five, recording a 55.5 and cutting the gap to Silkunas to just over two seconds. As she kept chipping away at Silkunas’s lead lap by lap, the margin was under a second by lap nine.

Fluxa’s charge through the middle portion of the race put Silkunas under pressure: by lap 10, she was just half a second behind the Lithuanian and she continuosly improved her fastest lap of the race—reaching a 55.288. However, as she prepared to mount a final attack, she started to lose pace with a couple of laps to go and Silkunas managed to hold her at bay with a flawless defensive drive.

Behind the leading group, Sofia Zanfari continued her charge, eventually finishing an impressive 11th after gaining ten places. Charlotte Page also had a standout race, climbing 12 positions to finish 12th, while Skye Parker and Elizaveta Kozlova completed their races in 13th and 15th, respectively.

![Image 5: ree](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/aed0c4_83b247d9447f439cb32ffd892eab0b74~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_147,h_92,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/aed0c4_83b247d9447f439cb32ffd892eab0b74~mv2.jpg)

Photo credits: RGMMC / F1 Academy

Despite falling short of the win, Fluxa’s second-place finish rounded out an extraordinary season. With six Final wins, nine podiums from 12 races, and a staggering 665 points, she secured the OK-N Senior class title in dominant fashion, leaving no doubt about her potential.

In the championship standings, British racer Skye Parker was the best classified female after Fluxa; despite joining the championship only at the Middle East rounds, she was still able to collect 82 points and finish 17th. Williams Academy's Sara Matsui moved to the Senior class after the European rounds but nevertheless finished 20th with 68 points.

Ella Lahdemaa had a strong start of the season but missed the last round, finishing 22nd. F1 Academy Discover Your Drive-supported driver Charlotte Page was P25 in the standings, ahead of Elizaveta Kozlova in P28, Sofia Zanfari in P30 and Payton Westcott in P35 - as the American, also supported by the F1 Academy programme, missed the second half of the season and started a testing programme in F4 machinery. Gianna Pascoal was P36, Yana Kapoor P38, and Anastasia Gerasis P41.

### Karting Champions League now welcoming 2026 Winter Series Entries

Drivers from the national and international realms of X30 and KZ karting are now welcome to enter the Winter Series of the 2026 Karting Champions League, the championship that offers the ideal way for everybody to get into a racing rhythm for the regular season.

### Numerous International Teams registered for the 24 Hours Karting of Italy

Just a few days after entries opened in early December, a strong number of teams have already registered for the 24 Hours Karting of Italy, promoted by CRG and scheduled for March 14–15 at the Castelletto di Branduzzo circuit (Italy). Several countries are already represented, with teams coming from China, the Czech Republic, Spain, Romania, France and Belgium, just to name the first registered entries. The 2026 edition is shaping up to have a clearly international profile in both admitted categories: PRO, dedicated to more experienced teams, and SILVER, designed for more amateur crews with all drivers over 18 years of age.

### 2025 Prokart Challenge Championship podium finishers honored

The 21st season of the ProKart Challenge concluded this past October, completing the five events with six rounds of competition for the Superkarts! USA regional program. Eleven different class champions were crowned following the action at the K1 Circuit finale event.

### ROK Cup Italia 2026 – calendar change

The 2025 ROK season came to the end with the Rok Festival, which took place on November 29 and 30 at the Franciacorta Karting Track, and now all attention is on the 2026 ROK calendar.

### 24 Hours Spa Karting: twice rather than once in 2026!

The 24 Hours Spa Karting is returning! Although the 2025 edition could not take place, organiser One Day Karting has decided to make up for it in 2026 with two events: one with a Sodikart fleet on 13 and 14 June, followed by a second with the traditional Biz Le Mans Twins on 5 and 6 September. Each with their own unique characteristics, these two events complement each other and both promise to be exciting and international.

USA Winter Series has been situated in the state of Florida, hosting events at Ocala Gran Prix, AMR Homestead-Miami Motorplex Presented by MG Tires and, most recently, the Orlando Kart Center. Each venue has provided its own uniqueness and history throughout the eight years of the program. Year nine of the SKUSA Winter Series will present a new location, with both events of the 2026 schedule to be held at the Speedsportz Racing Park in New Caney, Texas.

### A major sporting and organizational success for the 2025 Rental Kart World Contest

New format, same outstanding success for one of the most prestigious events in CRG’s Rental calendar: the Rental Kart World Contest. The 2025 edition of this renowned international meeting, raced with CRG Centurion karts, took place at the 7 Laghi Kart Track in Castelletto di Branduzzo, Italy, from October 17th to 19th. For this 6th edition, the race format brought back a mix of Sprint Cup and Endurance Cup, as it was in the inaugural 2016 event. Castelletto hosted the Sprint titles on Saturday — with over 100 drivers competing across Junior, Silver, and Pro categories — and the Endurance Cup on Sunday, a 6-hour race featuring 34 teams on the grid.

Published: 07 February 2025

Columns: Close Up

In a constantly evolving landscape, the FIA motorsport ladder is strengthening the connection between grassroots categories and the highest levels of competition. The Champions of the Future Academy Program, now entering its second full season, fits into this scenario with an innovative model based on inclusion, cost efficiency, and equal competition opportunities.

**A growth model for motorsport**  
The Champions of the Future Academy program has quickly gained a prominent role in the motorsport scene. In a sector where the connection between karting and Formula 1 is becoming increasingly direct, the initiative promoted by RGMMC stands out due to several key factors: inclusion, controlled costs through a fixed budget, and fair competition, ensured by the use of identical equipment for all participants.

**Expanding beyond traditional boundaries**  
One of the program’s most innovative aspects is the geographical expansion of karting, bringing the discipline to countries where motorsport is rapidly growing. This ambitious effort, successfully managed by the RGMMC team, has contributed to a broader dissemination of the sport and created new opportunities for young talents.

![Image 1](https://www.vroomkart.com/sites/vroomkart.com/files/ckeditor/images/FB.png)

**Female inclusion in Motorsport**  
The Academy has also achieved significant results in terms of female participation. For the first time, an international-level trophy was won by a female driver, and women now make up 30% of the participants. This concrete achievement reflects a real shift beyond mere discussions about the role of women in motorsport.

![Image 2](https://www.vroomkart.com/sites/vroomkart.com/files/ckeditor/images/RBAV_241204_COTFA_ALFORSAN_5347-scaled.jpg)

**A broad foundation for a competitive Future**  
The program aims to make motorsport more accessible by increasing the number of participants. This approach is already showing results, supported by key figures such as Susie Wolff, whose consistent presence at events serves as a strong incentive for young female drivers.

**Equal conditions in competition**  
The world of karting has undergone significant changes in recent years, with the “arrive and drive” model becoming the standard. In this context, RGMMC has created a fair competitive environment where drivers can showcase their talent without having to switch teams to remain competitive. This setup helps young drivers develop the ability to maximize their available resources, an essential skill for those aiming for higher levels.

![Image 3](https://www.vroomkart.com/sites/vroomkart.com/files/ckeditor/images/isack-hadjar2.jpg)

#### Isack Hadjar was present as a coach in Dubai

**Inspiration from the Champions of the Future**  
The presence of drivers from higher categories, such as Formula 2 and the F1 Academy, in the paddock serves as an additional source of motivation for young talents. Figures like Isack Hadjar provide practical advice and share their experiences, creating a direct bridge between the new generation and industry professionals.

Champions of the Future Academy Program
---------------------------------------

**Powered by RGMMC**

The _Champions of the Future Academy Program_ is a premier **Arrive and Drive** international karting series designed to develop the next generation of motorsport talent. Created by RGMMC and aligned with FIA sporting standards, the program combines elite competition with comprehensive driver education—offering young racers the experience and global exposure needed to launch professional careers while **controlling costs.**

Featuring three competitive categories—**Mini 60**, **OK-N Junior**, and **OK-N Senior**—the Academy brings together rising stars from around the world to compete in world-class events across the globe. Including on-track racing, physical training, workshops, and media day, making it a complete development platform for future champions.

Whether you’re an aspiring driver or sponsor, the Champions of the Future Academy is where the next generation begins.

![Image 18](https://www.championskartingacademy.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/SWTransparent1.png)

Discover Your Drive  
  
“With so much momentum building around F1 Academy, we must continue to strengthen the pipeline of talent coming into our sport. We look forward to this collaboration with Champions of The Future which will create a clear pathway from karting into F1 Academy. COTFA will operate a lottery system for the chassis and engines plus implement a fixed budget, giving us the opportunity to identify the top talent across all age groups. We will also provide the best in the senior category with an F1 Academy test, giving them a chance to prove themselves to our teams. Champions of the Future shares F1 Academy’s vision to increase female participation, create opportunity and allow clear progression up the motorsport ladder.”

Susie Wolff

Managing Director of F1 Academy

### why race cotfa?

The **Champions of the Future Academy Program** is designed to offer young drivers a world-class racing experience with a strong focus on development, exposure, and affordability. Here’s why it stands out:

### 🏁 **Elite Competition**

Compete against top young talents from across the globe in a highly professional and competitive environment, using CIK-FIA homologated material.

### 🌍 **International Exposure**

Race at renowned circuits and gain visibility in front of sponsors, and talent scouts from higher motorsport categories.

### 💸 **Cost-Controlled & Affordable**

The Academy Program is structured with **strict cost controls** to ensure fair competition and **keep participation costs relatively low** compared to other international karting series. This makes it an ideal choice for families and teams looking for maximum value without compromising on quality.

### 📈 **Career Development**

The program serves as a proven pathway to higher levels of motorsport, including OK/OKJ, FIA Karting, and even Formula 4. Many successful drivers have been on this journey.

### 🧠 **Education & Growth**

Drivers receive not only race experience but also lessons from Formula medicine  and media professionalism—all vital for a successful career.

### 🔧 **Top-Level Equipment**

Access to competitive, well-maintained karts, engines, and technical support, ensuring a level playing field for all participants.

### 🤝 **Networking & Support**

Build lasting connections with teams, coaches, and industry professionals who can support your progress through the motorsport ranks.

### whats the weekend format?

*   Thursday collection of material
*   Friday free practice all day
*   Saturday – Free practice, time qualifying, 2 heats and a Final
*   Sunday – Free practice, time qualifying, 2 heats and a Final

### F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE SELECTION PROCESS

*   We are looking for talented drivers with experience in karting to represent F1 Academy Discover Your Drive at the Champions of the Future Academy Program 2025.

*   3 drivers in each class will be selected to represent F1 Academy Discover Your Drive and receive a 30% discount on entry fees.

*   To be eligible for the selection process you must sign up before the 22nd of December to the 2025 Champions of the Future Academy Program.

*   If you don’t get selected for 2025 you can still compete in the Champions of the Future Academy Program, improve your skills and try again at the end of 2025.

### What is the material used

The Champions of the Future Academy Program elected chassis and engine suppliers will be Parolin powered by TM Kart Engines for the Mini class, and Kart Republic powered by IAME for the Junior and Senior classes.

### How do we ensure fair play

Ensuring equal material and fairness is the highest priority of the series. After each day all the engines are returned to the manufacturer to be checked and re-distributed via a lottery.

The manufacturers are onsite to provide technical support and help you with any quesitons you may have.

### Whats included in the package?

Those drivers signed up for the year receive a race suit, kart, awning space, trolley and work bench, tires and fuel.

The driver must provide their own mechanic and tools. Onsite we have tools such as drills and flat benches.

Click here for more information.") From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Champions of the Future
CategoryKart racing
RegionEurope
AffiliationsCIK-FIA

ClassesOK, OK-J, KZ, KZ2, KZ2-M, OK-N, OKN-J, 60 Mini

Official websiteOfficial website
**Champions of the Future** (**COTF**) is a [kart racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kart_racing "Kart racing") competition organised by the RGMMC Group and sanctioned by [FIA Karting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA_Karting "FIA Karting") (CIK-FIA). Founded in 2020, COTF is one of 11 competitions on the [international kart racing calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_kart_racing_championships#Active_international_championships "List of kart racing championships") in [CIK-FIA classes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_Internationale_de_Karting#Categories "Commission Internationale de Karting"). Initially a two-round series in [OK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF2 "KF2") and [OK-Junior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK-Junior "OK-Junior") (OK-J)—with single-round finals in [KZ2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2 "KZ2") and [60 Mini](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=60_Mini&action=edit&redlink=1 "60 Mini (page does not exist)")—the championship has since expanded to all eight CIK-FIA classes across the: **Euro Series** ([OK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF2 "KF2"), [OK-J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF3 "KF3")), **Shifters** ([KZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ_/(karting/) "KZ (karting)"), [KZ2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2 "KZ2"), [KZ2-M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2-M "KZ2-M")), and **Academy Program** ([OK-N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK-N "OK-N"), [OKN-J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OKN-J "OKN-J"), [60 Mini](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=60_Mini&action=edit&redlink=1 "60 Mini (page does not exist)")), the latter supported by [F1 Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F1_Academy "F1 Academy"). COTF also hosted the one-off **Winter Series** at [Franciacorta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autodromo_di_Franciacorta "Autodromo di Franciacorta") in 2022. COTF is set to expand to national series in 2026, hosting a British title with [Motorsport UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorsport_UK "Motorsport UK"), an [Emirati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") title, a [Macanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macau "Macau") title, and an [American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") title. The Euro Series and Shifters events traditionally take place in the two weeks prior to a [World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_World_Championship "Karting World Championship") or [European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_European_Championship "Karting European Championship") round at the same [circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kart_circuit "Kart circuit"). Notable former champions include [Nikita Bedrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Bedrin "Nikita Bedrin") (2020, OK), [Arvid Lindblad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arvid_Lindblad "Arvid Lindblad") (2020, OK-J), [Rafael Câmara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_C%C3%A2mara "Rafael Câmara") (2021, OK), [Freddie Slater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Slater_/(racing_driver/) "Freddie Slater (racing driver)") (2021, OK-J), [Alex Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Powell "Alex Powell") (2023, OK), and [Dries Van Langendonck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dries_Van_Langendonck "Dries Van Langendonck") (2024, OK-J). [Luna Fluxá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luna_Flux%C3%A1 "Luna Fluxá") (2024, OK-N) is the only [female driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_racing_drivers "List of female racing drivers") to win a title. ### Background (1962–2019) \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Champions_of_the_Future&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Background (1962–2019)")\] [![Image 11: The pre-grid of the 2015 KZ World Championship at Le Mans](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/KZ_PREGRID_KSP_6_7810-edit-660x330.jpg/250px-KZ_PREGRID_KSP_6_7810-edit-660x330.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:KZ_PREGRID_KSP_6_7810-edit-660x330.jpg) The RGMMC Group has been the official [promoter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promoter_/(entertainment/) "Promoter (entertainment)") of [CIK-FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIK-FIA "CIK-FIA") events—the [World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_World_Championship "Karting World Championship") and [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_European_Championship "Karting European Championship") Championships—since 2018. The [Commission Internationale de Karting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_Internationale_de_Karting "Commission Internationale de Karting") (CIK-FIA) was founded in 1962 by the [Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_de_l%27Automobile "Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile") (FIA) to govern the rising international sport of [kart racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kart_racing "Kart racing").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-1) The inaugural [CIK-FIA World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIK-FIA_World_Championship "CIK-FIA World Championship") was hosted two years later at the _[Pista d'Oro](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pista_d%27Oro&action=edit&redlink=1 "Pista d'Oro (page does not exist)")_ in [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome"), which again held the event in 1965.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-2) The CIK-FIA began its [homologation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homologation_/(motorsport/) "Homologation (motorsport)") of distinct classes in the discipline in 1974, when the first 125 cc [gearbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gearbox "Gearbox") category was created for the [European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_European_Championship "Karting European Championship"): [Formula C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ_/(karting/) "KZ (karting)") (FC).[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-3) The 100 cc [direct-drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct-drive "Direct-drive") category was clarified in 1976, when [Formula Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF1 "KF1") was introduced to control technical evolutions and costs.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-4) The direct-drive classes were adapted in 1981, when the 135 cc [Formula K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_K "Formula K") (FK), 100 cc [Intercontinental A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_A "Intercontinental A") (ICA), and [Junior Intercontinental A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_Intercontinental_A "Junior Intercontinental A") (ICA-J) were introduced to the World Championship, European Championship, and [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_World_Cup "Karting World Cup"), respectively.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-5) By 2020, there were five [CIK-FIA classes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_Internationale_de_Karting#Categories "Commission Internationale de Karting"): [OK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF2 "KF2"), the primary senior direct-drive class; [OK-Junior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK-Junior "OK-Junior") (OK-J), the under-15 direct-drive class; [KZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ_/(karting/) "KZ (karting)"), the primary gearbox class; [KZ2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2 "KZ2"), the secondary gearbox class; and [60 Mini](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=60_Mini&action=edit&redlink=1 "60 Mini (page does not exist)"), the under-12 international class.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-7) [Rotax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotax "Rotax") was founded in 1920 as an [internal combustion engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_combustion_engine "Internal combustion engine") manufacturer and entered the FK class in 1983,[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-8) later founding the [Rotax Max Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotax_Max_Challenge "Rotax Max Challenge") in 2000.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-9) [Italian American Motor Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_American_Motor_Engineering "Italian American nine drivers in both the British and Emirati series for a total of 27.[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-F12025-69) The **Champions of the Future America Series** (**COTFAS**) is set to debut across 10 rounds from January to September in partnership with [K1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K1_Speed "K1 Speed") at [K1 Circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=K1_Circuit&action=edit&redlink=1 "K1 Circuit (page does not exist)") in [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") and [Spring Mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_Mountain_Motorsports_Ranch "Spring Mountain Motorsports Ranch") in [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada").[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-US-72) The inaugural edition of COTF held four-day weekends: [free practice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_motorsport_terms#F "Glossary of motorsport terms") sessions on the Thursday and Friday mornings, qualifying practice on Friday afternoon, qualifying [heats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_motorsport_terms#H "Glossary of motorsport terms") on Saturday and Sunday mornings, and pre-finals/finals on the Sunday afternoon.[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-VK2020-73) The registration fees were [€](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro")495 per round for [60 Mini](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=60_Mini&action=edit&redlink=1 "60 Mini (page does not exist)") and €595 for [OK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF2 "KF2"), [OK-J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK-J "OK-J"), and [KZ2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2 "KZ2").[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-VK2020-73) By 2024, the round fees increased to €675 for the Euro Series and Shifters, with an additional €100 charge for free practice.[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-74)[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-75) The season fees for the [arrive-and-drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_motorsport_terms#A "Glossary of motorsport terms") Academy Program that year were €29,000 ([OK-N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK-N "OK-N") and [OKN-J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OKN-J "OKN-J")) and €23,000 (60 Mini),[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-AP2024-43) including a new [chassis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chassis "Chassis"), [engines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engine "Engine"), [tyres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyres "Tyres"), fuel, a [paddock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_motorsport_terms#P "Glossary of motorsport terms") area, logistical support, travel, and accommodation.[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-76) As of 2025, the Euro Series is held over a three-day weekend composed of free practice (FP), time trials (TT), qualifying heats (QH), super heats (SH), and the finals:[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-77) * Thursday: FP + TT (morning), QH (afternoon); * Friday: warm-up + QH; * Saturday: warm-up + SH (morning), [OK-J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK-J "OK-J") and [OK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF2 "KF2") final (afternoon). The Euro Series follows the general [CIK-FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIK-FIA "CIK-FIA") points system, with a maximum of: 25 for QH, 25 for SH, and 50 for finals; [dead heats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_heat "Dead heat") are settled via [count-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_motorsport_terms#C "Glossary of motorsport terms") in finals.[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-78)[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-FIA2025-79) As of 2025, Shifters is held over a three-day weekend composed of free practice (FP), qualifying practice (QP), qualifying heats (QH), super heats (SH), and the finals:[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-80) * Thursday: FP (morning), QP (afternoon); * Friday: warm-up + QH; * Saturday: warm-up + SH (morning), [KZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ_/(karting/) "KZ (karting)") and [KZ2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2 "KZ2") final (afternoon). Shifters follows the general CIK-FIA points system, with a maximum of: 25 for QH, 25 for SH, and 50 for finals; dead heats are settled via count-back in finals.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-81)[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-FIA2025-79) As of 2025, the Academy Program is held over a three-day weekend composed of free practice (FP), qualifying practice (QP), qualifying heats (QH), and two finals in each class:[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-82) * Friday: FP; * Saturday: FP + QP + QH (morning), [OKN-J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OKN-J "OKN-J"), [60 Mini](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=60_Mini&action=edit&redlink=1 "60 Mini (page does not exist)"), and [OK-N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK-N "OK-N") final one (afternoon); * Sunday: FP + QP + QH (morning), OKN-J, 60 Mini, and OK-N final two (afternoon). The Academy Program follows the general CIK-FIA points system, with a maximum of: 25 for QH and 50 for finals; dead heats are settled via count-back in finals.[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-83)[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-FIA2025-79) [![Image 16: Aerial photograph of Steel Ring Třinec in 2020](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Steel_Ring_Trzyniec.jpg/250px-Steel_Ring_Trzyniec.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Steel_Ring_Trzyniec.jpg) In the 2023 Euro Series, [Třinec](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steel_Ring_T%C5%99inec&action=edit&redlink=1 "Steel Ring Třinec (page does not exist)") became the first Czech circuit to feature in [CIK-FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIK-FIA "CIK-FIA") competition since the 1990s. Published: 19 March 2020

Columns: Races

RGMMC has changed the dates for the first season of its brand new "Champions of the Future".

Due to Covid-19 emergency, RGMMC has changed the dates of its Champions of the Future championship.

The opening round is programmed from May 7 to 10 in Germany, before the FIA Karting OK and OKJ European Championship.

The series will continue in Sweden, at the Åsum Ring, from 25 to 28 June. The closing round is scheduled in Zuera, from 16 to 19 July.

RGMMC's statement:

_«As round one is scheduled to take place at the beginning of May the entries will be open until the 27th of April. On the 27th of April we will review the situation to confirm the event. No payment will be required in order to make an entry until 100% confirmation of the event.»_

**Applications are now open for young karters to sign up for the 2026 Champions of the Future Academy Program International Series, with F1 ACADEMY also looking for talented young female karters to represent F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE in the series next year.**

### HOW DOES THE SERIES WORK?

Designed to develop the next generation of motorsport talent, the Champions of the Future Academy Program is an Arrive and Drive karting program featuring three mixed gender age categories, Mini 60 (ages 8-12), OK-N Junior (ages 11-14) and OK-N Senior (ages 14-17), competing in equal equipment.

The Mini class will run Parolin chassis powered by TM Kart Engines, while Kart Republic chassis powered by IAME will be run by the Junior and Senior classes. COTFA aims to break down barriers to entry by featuring cost control measures, including a limit on entry fees alongside a chassis and engine lottery.

Each round runs on a four-day format with the collection of material taking place on Thursday, followed by all-day Free Practice on Friday. Saturday and Sunday each feature Free Practice, Time qualifying, two heats and a Final.

### WHERE WILL COTFA BE RACING IN 2026?

1.  Kartodromo Internacional Lucas Guerrero, Valencia, Spain (March 6 – 8)
2.  Circuit 27, Thessaloniki, Greece (May 29 – 31)
3.  Leopard Circuit Viterbo, Viterbo, Italy (July 17 – 19)
4.  Muscat Speedway, Muscat, Oman (October 30 – November 1)
5.  Al Ain Raceway, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (November 23 – 25)
6.  Al Forsan International Sports Resort, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (November 30 – December 2)

### WHY APPLY TO REPRESENT F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE?

Following on from the success across the 2024 and 2025 seasons, applications are also now open to represent F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE in the 2026 Champions of the Future Academy Program International. Up to three female karters in each age category (totalling nine karters) will be supported.

**All F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE applicants will receive:**

*   A hard copy of the [Driver Development Guide](https://www.f1academy.com/latest/oopmXRq6TdWMHlrsYTTGN/driver-development-guide)
*   Access to F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE events and experiences throughout the year, including;
    *   [Virtual Driver Development Workshops](https://www.f1academy.com/Discover-Your-Drive/3hMiBthv4ebh3G0cGoDJ2R/f1-academy-driver-development-workshop-series)
    *   Driver Development face-to-face workshop with F1 ACADEMY Performance and Talent Development Manager, Katie Denver, at the first International and UK round of COTFA
    *   Access to in person events held throughout the year – locations to be confirmed at a later date
    *   Driver CV added to the F1 ACADEMY Driver Talent database for future consideration

**For those drivers successfully selected to represent F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE in 2026, in addition to the above they will receive:**

*   F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE Branded race suit, gloves, boots and shirts
*   F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVER Branded kart livery
*   Financial contribution towards entry fees (30% discount contributed by RGMMC)
*   Development support and guidance throughout the year from F1 ACADEMY’s Performance and Talent Development Team

### HOW TO SIGN UP FOR COTFA?

Karters who meet the age criteria can sign up for the series via the [Champions of the Future Academy website](https://www.championskartingacademy.com/). To be apply for F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE support, you need to submit your racing CV to COTFA by January 12. Applications will be reviewed and selected drivers notified by January 16. Applications made after January 12 will not be considered.

F1 ACADEMY expands support for Champions of The Future Academy for 2026
=======================================================================

F1 ACADEMY has announced the renewal and expansion of its support for global karting series Champions of The Future Academy.

![Image 51: JAZ_9752-Avec%20accentuation-Bruit.jpg](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9Centre/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000000/fom-website/2025/F1%20Academy/JAZ_9752-Avec%20accentuation-Bruit.webp)

F1 ACADEMY has announced the renewal and expansion of its support for global karting series Champions of The Future Academy (COTFA), with up to 27 young female drivers set to be supported by F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE in 2026.

Since its launch in 2023, COTFA has made significant strides in increasing female participation, with the percentage of female drivers on the grid rising from 5% in its inaugural year to an impressive 30% in 2025, an incredible leap that reflects the growing impact that COTFA and F1 ACADEMY are having on the future female talent pool.

As part of its continued global expansion, COTFA has introduced two new national initiatives, which will serve as regional feeder series to complement its international championship:

*   The Champions of the Future Academy Program UAE, with select participants supported by F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE, a two-round national karting championship running across 2025–2026.
*   The British Champions of the Future Academy Program, with select participants supported by F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE, launching in 2026, which will run across four rounds.

![Image 52: JAZ_8438%20-%20COTFA%20Portimao%20-%20Feb%2025%20-%20%40JazzVian-2.jpg](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000000/fom-website/2025/F1%20Academy/JAZ_8438%20-%20COTFA%20Portimao%20-%20Feb%2025%20-%20@JazzVian-2.webp)Up to 27 young female drivers are set to be supported by F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE in 2026

F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE will continue its support for nine drivers, three in each age category, in the International Initiative Champions of the Future Academy Program. Additionally, in expansion of this support, F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE will support up to nine drivers, up to three in each age category, in each of the new National Initiatives.

All selected drivers across the three initiatives will participate in F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE-branded karts and race suits. RGMMC – the motorsport event management company responsible for organising and promoting all COTFA initiatives – will also contribute a 30% discount towards each F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE participant’s entry fee.

Ahead of the opening round of the UAE Initiative, taking place from 7–9 November 2025, F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE is supporting six drivers. The six supported drivers for the Champions of the Future Academy Program UAE, with select participants supported by F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE 2025/2026 season, are:

Minis (ages 8-11)

*   Khloe McGill
*   Atiqa Mir \*DYD COTFAP 2025

Juniors (ages 11-14)

*   Kalyani Pratheesh
*   Ilijana Ostojic

Seniors (ages 14-17)

*   Vanesa Silkunaite \*DYD COTFAP 2025
*   Ella Hakkinen \*DYD COTFAP 2025

Entries for the British Champions of the Future Academy Program, with select participants supported by F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE, open at the end of October, and aspiring drivers can apply via COTFA to be considered for F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE support.

Susie Wolff, Managing Director of F1 ACADEMY, said: “It’s incredible to see how quickly the level of female talent in this championship has risen. With everyone on the same specification equipment and a capped budget, it gives us a real sense of who stands out on merit alone. Our supported drivers aren’t just competing - they’re winning races and showing they have potential talent to rise into F1 Academy and beyond. We’re now extending our support to up to twenty-seven drivers across the international and new UAE and British series - reinforcing our commitment to growing the talent pool.”

James Geidel, Champions of the Future President, added: “It has been a great pleasure working alongside F1 Academy Discover Your Drive over the past two years. Together, we’ve made significant progress in increasing female participation, which now stands at an impressive 30%. With the launch of the Champions of the Future Academy Program and its national championships, we’re now able to support female talent from the grassroots level on a broader, global scale.”

Katie Denver, F1 ACADEMY Performance & Talent Development Manager, added: “The expansion of Champions of the Future Academy gives us a stronger platform to identify, support, and develop emerging talent from an earlier stage. The introduction of regional series in the UAE and UK marks a new chapter to make karting more accessible, competitive, and inclusive, especially for female talent.”

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia [![Image 1: The pre-grid of the 2015 KZ World Championship at Le Mans](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/KZ_PREGRID_KSP_6_7810-edit-660x330.jpg/250px-KZ_PREGRID_KSP_6_7810-edit-660x330.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:KZ_PREGRID_KSP_6_7810-edit-660x330.jpg) The [KZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ_/(karting/) "KZ (karting)") pre-final of the [Karting World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_World_Championship "Karting World Championship") in 2015 at [Le Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_de_la_Sarthe "Circuit de la Sarthe"), which was won by [Jorrit Pex](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jorrit_Pex&action=edit&redlink=1 "Jorrit Pex (page does not exist)") The following is a **list of international kart racing champions** in classes sanctioned by the [CIK-FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIK-FIA "CIK-FIA") since 2007, when [KF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF1 "KF1") and [KZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ_/(karting/) "KZ (karting)") regulations were introduced to [international competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_kart_racing_championships "List of kart racing championships").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-CIK2007-1) [Original Kart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Original_Kart "Original Kart") replaced KF as the [direct-drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct-drive "Direct-drive") regulation in 2016, also when [OK-Junior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK-Junior "OK-Junior") replaced its [KF-Junior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF-Junior "KF-Junior") counterpart.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-2) KZ—formerly known as _KZ1_—and [KZ2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2 "KZ2") have remained the [gearbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gearbox "Gearbox") classes.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-3) [Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_Academy_Trophy "Karting Academy Trophy") and [60 Mini](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=60_Mini&action=edit&redlink=1 "60 Mini (page does not exist)") have since been introduced as junior categories by the CIK-FIA in 2010 and 2020, respectively.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-60_Mini-5) Young drivers typically progress to [junior formulae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_formulae "Junior formulae") before reaching the gearbox classes—referred to as "the domain of [factory teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factory-backed "Factory-backed") and [professional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_sports "Professional sports") drivers" by the CIK-FIA—as the minimum age for progression has decreased throughout the 21st century.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-7) [IAME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_American_Motor_Engineering "Italian American Motor Engineering") classes also feature prominently on the international [kart racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kart_racing "Kart racing") calendar,[\[note 1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-8) as well as the [Rotax Max Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotax_Max_Challenge "Rotax Max Challenge") (2000–present) and [ROK Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ROK_Cup&action=edit&redlink=1 "ROK Cup (page does not exist)") (2003–present),[\[note 2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-9) which operate under [manufacturer-designated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factory-backed "Factory-backed") classes approved by the CIK-FIA.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-10) The inaugural editions of several competitions pre-date this list: [Karting World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_World_Championship "Karting World Championship") (1964),[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-11) [Karting European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_European_Championship "Karting European Championship") (1970),[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-12) [Trofeo delle Industrie](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Trofeo_delle_Industrie&action=edit&redlink=1 "Trofeo delle Industrie (page does not exist)") (1971),[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-13) [Karting Asia-Pacific Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Karting_Asia-Pacific_Championship&action=edit&redlink=1 "Karting Asia-Pacific Championship (page does not exist)") (1981),[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-14) [Andrea Margutti Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrea_Margutti_Trophy&action=edit&redlink=1 "Andrea Margutti Trophy (page does not exist)") (1990),[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-15) [CIK-FIA Viking Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=CIK-FIA_Viking_Trophy&action=edit&redlink=1 "CIK-FIA Viking Trophy (page does not exist)") (1990),[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-16) [Monaco Kart Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco_Kart_Cup "Monaco Kart Cup") (1995),[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-17) [South Garda Winter Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Garda_Winter_Cup&action=edit&redlink=1 "South Garda Winter Cup (page does not exist)") (1996),[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-18) and [WSK International Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=WSK_International_Series&action=edit&redlink=1 "WSK International Series (page does not exist)") (2006).[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-19) The [superkart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superkart "Superkart") category also pre-dates the list, reaching the international stage as early as 1976.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-20) Several national championships have also held international classes.[\[note 3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-25) [Marco Ardigò](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marco_Ardig%C3%B2&action=edit&redlink=1 "Marco Ardigò (page does not exist)") won a record 22 international titles from 2007—including three World and three European Championships—until his retirement in 2019,[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-Ardig%C3%B2-26) followed by [Max Verstappen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen "Max Verstappen")'s 13 titles from 2010 to 2013. Since 2007, Italian drivers have won 197 titles—96 of which are in the [gearbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gearbox "Gearbox") classes—with British drivers on 111, and Dutch drivers on 72. Three [women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_racing_drivers "List of female racing drivers") feature on this list: [Beitske Visser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beitske_Visser "Beitske Visser"),[\[note 4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-28) [Marta García](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marta_Garc%C3%ADa_/(racing_driver/) "Marta García (racing driver)"),[\[note 5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-31) and [Luna Fluxá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luna_Flux%C3%A1 "Luna Fluxá").[\[note 6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-33)

[KF1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF1 "KF1")—replaced by _Super-KF_ (SKF) from 2009 to 2010—was the primary [direct-drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct-drive "Direct-drive") class in CIK-FIA competition from 2007 to 2012 for drivers aged 15 and over.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-34)[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-35) _Super-KF_ differed from KF1 with [non-homologated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homologation_/(motorsport/) "Homologation (motorsport)") engines, whilst retaining the free [chassis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chassis "Chassis"), [brakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakes "Brakes"), and [tyres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyres "Tyres").[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_kart_racing_champions#cite_note-Categories-36) It hosted the [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_World_Championship "Karting World Championship") in each year of its existence bar 2010, where it was replaced by Champions of the Future America Announced
=========================================

02 [Featured](https://www.k1speed.com/blog/category/featured) December 02, 2025

[0](https://www.k1speed.com/blog/champions-of-the-future-america-announced.html# "Like this")

Share

![Image 4: The 10-race schedule for Champions of the Future America.](https://www.k1speed.com/blog/champions-of-the-future-america-announced.html)

WINCHESTER, Calif., December 2, 2025 — RGMMC Group, a global leader in international karting promotion and the organization behind the highly acclaimed “Champions of the Future” series, today announced a landmark partnership with K1 to launch **Champions of the Future America**, a new initiative designed to elevate the next generation of American motorsport talent and create new pathways through the sport.

This collaboration marks a major milestone in bringing a new format of competitive karting platform to the U.S. market, giving young American drivers access to the same professional standards, organization, technology, and competitive environment that have helped shape numerous current elite motorsport athletes.

“**America is the largest karting market**, and partnering with K1 allows us to bring a proven development pathway to a country with passion, scale, and talent. While bridging the gap between Europe and the United States,” said James Geidel, CEO of RGMMC.

K1, a recognized leader in American karting and motorsport entertainment since 2003 with brands K1 Speed and K1 Circuit, will bring its national footprint, industry knowledge, and strong community of young racers to the partnership. Together, RGMMC and K1 will introduce a series of events and programs focused on doing things differently.

**“K1’s ambition is to introduce casual indoor go-kart racers to the world of outdoor karting as part of the pathway to professional motorsport,**” said K1’s Founder and CEO, David Danglard. “By partnering with Champions of the Future in North America, we can achieve this goal and give our drivers the best opportunity to pursue their racing dreams.”

Race Series Features
--------------------

*   A professionally organized race series aligned with international standards
*   Pathways for U.S. drivers to access global karting competitions 
*   State-of-the-art event management and technological support

### 2026 Schedule

Rd 1 January 31- February 1 **K1 Circuit**

Rd 2 February 28 -March 1 **K1 Circuit**

Rd 3 March 21- 22 **K1 Circuit**

Rd 4 April 18-19 **K1 Circuit**

Rd 5 & 6 May 29-31 **Spring Mountain Double header 3 Day Event**

Rd 7 June 27-28 **K1 Circuit**

Rd 8 July 18-19 **K1 Circuit**

Rd 9 August 29-30 **K1 Circuit**

Rd 10 September 26-27 **K1 Circuit**

Categories to be included: Mini, IAME X30, KA100, and KZ classes.

**Kristianstad Hosts Thrilling Champions of the Future Euro Series Finale, Crowning Craigie and Baglin as Champions**

Kristianstad, Sweden, was the setting for the fifth and final round of the 2025 Champions of the Future Euro Series, held on September 7, 2025. The event, organised by RGMMC, brought together 204 of the best young international hopefuls and top teams for three days of intense competition on the largely dry Asum Ring. Tillotson Racing was the carburettor of choice for all competitors on the podium!

**OK Category: Kelleher Triumphs in Final, Craigie Secures Series Title**

In the **OK category**, Britain’s Kenzo Craigie (Prema Racing) arrived in Kristianstad as the series leader, closely pursued by Spain’s Christian Costoya (Parolin Motorsport) and Belgium’s Thibaut Ramaekers (VDK Racing). These three drivers dominated timed practice, with Craigie ultimately taking pole position.

Ramaekers emerged from the Qualifying Heats in the lead, securing four wins, while Costoya and Craigie each claimed three. Sweden’s Oliver Kinnmark (Koski Motorsport) and Ireland’s Daniel Kelleher (KR Motorsport) also impressed with two wins apiece, and Ukraine’s Lev Krutoholov (Energy Corse) added one win, finishing 6th. The intensity heightened in the Super Heats, where Craigie won the first, followed by Kinnmark and Ramaekers. Ramaekers then won the second, ahead of Britons Joe Turney (KR Motorsport) and Scott Marsh (DPK Racing).

The Final saw Ramaekers initially hold his lead, though Costoya and Kinnmark lost significant ground early on. On lap 11 of 25, Craigie seized an opportunity to pass Ramaekers, bringing Kelleher with him. A dozen laps later, Kelleher continued his charge, taking the lead and ultimately racing to a superb victory. Despite Kelleher’s win, Craigie’s performance secured him the **Champions of the Future Euro Series title for 2025**, a year after his compatriot Joe Turney achieved the same feat.

Ramaekers finished 3rd on the podium in Kristianstad, placing him three points ahead of Costoya for the runner-up spot in the series. Other notable finishers in the final included Britain’s Turney (KR Motorsport) in 4th, followed by his team-mates Jacob Micallef (Malta) and Iacopo Martinese (Italy). Britons Zac Drummond and Jesse Phillips (Fusion Motorsport) finished 7th and 8th respectively. Indonesia’s Qarrar Firhand (Ward Racing) and Italy’s Gino Rocchio (Monster K Factory Team), who also set the fastest lap, completed the top 10.

The final OK series standings show **Kenzo Craigie (GBR) as champion with 333 points**, followed by Thibaut Ramaekers (BEL) with 277 points and Christian Costoya (ESP) with 274 points. Daniel Kelleher (IRL) finished 4th with 238 points, and Joe Turney (GBR) was 5th with 234 points. All competitors in this category used Maxxis tyres.

**OK-Junior Category: Baglin’s Double Victory Secures Series Title**

In the **OK-Junior category**, the series standings before Kristianstad were tight, with Australia’s William Calleja (Forza Racing) leading on 271 points, followed by Canada’s Ilie Crisan (Tony Kart Racing Team) with 259 points, and Britain’s Noah Baglin (Prema Racing) with 240 points. Britain’s Evan Purcell (RFM) took pole position, ahead of American Michael McGaughy (Koski Motorsport).

McGaughy dominated the Qualifying Heats, winning all five and taking the lead in the standings after this stage, ahead of Emiliano Hernandez (DPK Racing). Other winners in the heats included Baglin, Crisan, Purcell, Dutchman Dean Hoogendoorn (Prema Racing), Valerio Viapana (Koski Motorsport), and Argentina’s Martin Bertolaccini (Ward Racing).

McGaughy continued his strong form by winning the first Super Heat ahead of Frenchman Luka Scelles (VictoryLane). Finland’s Oskari Walle (Parolin Motorsport) confirmed his rise by winning the second Super Heat, ahead of Turkey’s Iskender Zulfikari (Forza Racing).

In the Final, Baglin executed his strategy perfectly. Starting 2nd behind McGaughy on the first lap, he seized the lead on the second lap and eventually pulled away from American Devin Walz (KR Motorsport) and Walle, who tried to keep pace. With Calleja failing to score points and Crisan finishing 12th, **Baglin secured a double victory, winning the Final and being crowned the Champions of the Future Euro Series OK-Junior champion**, succeeding Belgium’s Dries Van Langendonck. He finished ahead of Calleja and Crisan in the overall standings.

Dean Hoogendoorn made an impressive climb from 18th to 2nd place in the Final, but a penalty relegated him to 8th. After McGaughy crashed out in 10th, Walz won the battle for 2nd place on the Kristianstad podium, ahead of Walle and Scelles. Zulfikari finished 5th, while Zdenek Babicek (Tepz Racing Team) made an exceptional gain of 15 places. Bertolaccini and Frenchman Matéo Rivals (Tony Kart Racing Team) also finished in the top 10, in 8th and 9th positions respectively.

The final OK-Junior series standings show **Noah Baglin (GBR) as champion with 309 points**, followed by William Calleja (AUS) with 271 points and Ilie Tristan Crisan (CAN) with 265 points. Henry Domain (GBR) was 4th with 213 points, and Dean Hoogendoorn (NED) 5th with 178 points. All competitors in this category also used Maxxis tyres.

Motorsport UK British Champions of the Future Academy Programme revealed for 2026
=================================================================================

Friday 10 January 2025

Motorsport UK in conjunction with RGMMC, a global promoter of karting events, have launched a new global concept for drivers to showcase their talent using supplied equipment: The 2026 Motorsport UK British Champions of the Future Academy Programme.

This innovation not only opens doors for aspiring drivers but also expands karting to those who may not own their own equipment, making the sport more accessible to drivers and families.

The Champions of the Future Academy Programme, organised by RGMMC, saw opening seasons events take place in the Middle East and Europe, with the series set to land in the UK in 2026.

The new Academy Programme will take place at four UK locations in 2026**.** Drivers will be able to compete in three classes; the Mini 60, Ages 8 – 12 (chassis – Parolin powered by TM), OK-N Junior, Ages 12-14 (chassis – Kart Republic powered by IAME) and OK-N Senior Ages 15 plus (chassis – Kart Republic powered by IAME) classes. All karts and engines are drawn by lottery for each event.

In the ever-evolving world of motorsport, the pursuit of more diverse racing opportunities and the discovery of promising talent are vital for the sport’s growth and sustainability.

The new series also acknowledges the growing number of drivers joining the sport from Motorsport UK’s “Arrive and Drive” Championships and forms another critical step in the Karting Pathway, which was established in 2020.

As part of the introduction of this new Championship, Motorsport UK will also launch a dedicated Motorsport UK Academy specifically for karting, which will include a programme specifically for female drivers.

In 2025, female drivers are set to make up over 30% of the Champions of the Future (COTF) programme, a foundation we aim to build upon when the Academy Championship launches in the UK in 2026.

Dan Parker, Head of Karting, Motorsport UK, comments, “We are proud to launch the Motorsport UK Academy Championship in the UK in 2026, in collaboration with RGMMC. This groundbreaking initiative is designed to showcase and build on the immense talent of drivers in the UK using internationally recognised FIA-homologated supplied equipment.

“With four double-header events scheduled for the season, the series will feature three categories, a format that not only levels the playing field but also opens the doors of the sport to those who may not own their own kart equipment.

“The Academy Series provides another vital step in the Karting Pathway, which Motorsport UK established in 2020, in addition to the launch of our programme that is specifically for female drivers, underscoring our commitment to fostering diversity in the sport.”

James Geidel, President of the RGMMC Group, adds, “We are delighted to have our first national series launching in 2026 in collaboration with Motorsport UK. The United Kingdom is famed for being the home of motorsport and has an incredibly healthy karting culture. This is a true example of Motorsport UK’s forward-thinking to grow karting and this championship, ensuring that both aspiring drivers and their families can engage with the sport in new and exciting ways.”

Champions of the Future Academy to launch in the UK for 2026, offering further opportunities for Karting talent
===============================================================================================================

Tuesday 15 July 2025

This National Motorsport Week karting is a motorsport discipline that definitely deserves a mention! It’s pretty well-known that, barring a few exceptions, most of today’s top professional racing drivers all started their careers in karting.

2026 will see even more opportunities for aspiring drivers to get involved in karting, if they lack current access to high performance FIA karting equipment through: The 2026 Motorsport UK British Champions of the Future Academy Programme.

Launched in conjunction with RGMMC, a global promoter of karting events, the programme has had successful seasons in Europe and the Middle East.

Arriving in the UK in 2026, the programme will take place at four UK locations, with drivers able to compete in three classes; the Mini 60, Ages 8 – 12 (chassis – Parolin powered by TM), OK-N Junior, Ages 12-14 (chassis – Kart Republic powered by IAME) and OK-N Senior Ages 15 to 18 (chassis – Kart Republic powered by IAME) classes. All karts and engines are drawn by lottery.

The new series also acknowledges the growing number of drivers joining the sport from Motorsport UK’s “Arrive and Drive” Championships and forms another critical step in the Karting Pathway, which was established in 2020.

Buoyed on by the successful launch of [Motorsport UK’s Girls Karting Academy](https://www.motorsportuk.org/about-us/equality-diversity-and-inclusion/initiatives/girls-karting-academy/), it is expected that female drivers are set to make up over 30% of the Champions of the Future (COTF) programme, a foundation which will continue to be built upon next year.

James Geidel, President of the RGMMC Group, adds, “Following the success and validation of the Champions of the Future Academy Program International Series, the platform has firmly established itself as a launchpad for future stars in motorsport.

“Our very first Junior winner, James Anagnostiadis, was signed to the Mercedes Driver Development Programme, and just nine months later went on to become Vice Champion at the FIA Karting World Championship. Similarly, Sara Matsui earned a place in the Williams Racing Driver Academy, and Fionn McLaughlin was recruited by Red Bull Racing. These achievements underscore the Academy’s strength as a genuine talent identification platform.

“In addition, our close collaboration with the F1 Academy’s “Discover Your Drive” initiative will now extend into our national-level programmes.

“The United Kingdom, long regarded as one of the world’s premier environments for nurturing young racing talent, is the natural home for the launch of the Champions of the Future Academy Program National Series. This expansion marks an exciting new chapter in our mission to develop the next generation of racing talent.”

Dan Parker, Head of Karting, Motorsport UK, comments, “In the ever-evolving world of motorsport, the pursuit of more diverse racing opportunities and supporting promising talent are vital for the sport’s growth and sustainability.

“With four double-header events scheduled for the season, and three categories, there are now even more opportunities for aspiring talent to get involved and try out Karting for themselves.”
